_about: The only hand-written half of the component data. Everything else in _data/components.json is generated from the plugin source by _tools/compdata.py. English only - this file ships to the public repo.

Dim Styl.note: A Rhino dimension style, wired from a Rhino object parameter. Leave it unwired for the default style.

D.note: Data Gate holds a wire shut, so this input takes whatever the component upstream of it makes.

Results.note: Table Out takes any mix of result objects - section, analysis, seat map or C-value map. Anything with no table form is skipped.

_selfchain_about: Components that can be wired into another copy of themselves in series. Port types alone cannot tell this apart from an accidental loop, so each entry is declared here with the note the chain box shows. Only components whose own output type matches one of their own input types may be listed - compdata.py fails the build otherwise.

selfchain.cut: Chains into another Cut. Two in series with complementary Tier Enabled is how you cut different tiers from opposite sides.
selfchain.opening-cut: Chains into another Opening Cut. Every stage of the cut chain can be skipped or repeated.

_notes_about: Per-component paragraph, shown as 'What it does' below the port tables. Written by hand for the components whose behavior is not visible in their ports - a rule that belongs to one port goes in that port's tooltip in the plugin source instead, so Grasshopper shows it too. One paragraph, no markup - the template escapes it. English only, like the rest of this file. compdata.py fails the build on a key that is not a component id.

notes.cut: A seat, aisle cell or vomitory goes only when it crosses into the side being removed - one that merely touches the cut line stays. So a cut line drawn on top of a tread ring or an axis line keeps the seats that hang on that line. A cut line drawn exactly on an axis line also leaves a narrow empty strip beside it: seats are laid out between axis lines, the leftover width gathers at the axis, and the seat that straddles the line goes with the cut. End Aisle clears seats and nothing else; on a curve that runs along a row it empties that whole row. On a closed start line the axis numbers run counterclockwise whichever way the line was drawn - read them off View Axis before filling in Axis From and Axis To. With Cut End Mode EXTEND, a row that runs through a vomitory where the cut is made stays open to the new end face: no seats are laid in its extension.
notes.custom-seat: A tier given all three of vomitories, aisle cells and seats is taken as complete, and Custom Seat adds nothing of its own there - no automatic aisle beside a vomitory and no aisle carried up to the top row - so every aisle you want has to be drawn. Aisle cells drawn inside a vomitory passage or its entry band are removed, with an orange warning that gives the row and position. A tier missing any of the three is filled in as before: the component adds the aisles and seats it needs. Wheelchair spaces are optional either way.
notes.table-section: Each tier's start point comes from the workbook's 12_INPUT_TIER page as start_mode, start_h and start_v. PREV_TIER, the default above tier 0, measures from the outer end of the lower tier's last tread - the edge away from the field - at that tread's top surface, not from its nosing or a railing top. The upper tier's first tread front edge then sits start_h outward (negative when it overhangs the tier below) and start_v up, so start_v alone sets the height between tiers and the lower tier's last riser height is not used. START_LINE, the default for tier 0, measures from the start line's anchor point - 0, 0 puts the first tread front edge on the start line - and FOCAL measures from the focal point. Section Plus then moves the whole section outward by tier 0's solid_thickness, which keeps the tiers where they are relative to each other. To take the values off a drawing: start_v is the top of the upper tier's first tread minus the top of the lower tier's last tread, and start_h is the horizontal distance from the lower tier's last tread outer end to the upper tier's first tread front edge, negative toward the field.
notes.sheet-setup: One Sheet Setup can feed C-value Map, C-value Section Check and Seat Map, but each of them works out its own scale: the most detailed one its drawing fits at on the sheet, rounded up to a multiple of Scale Step. Enter the scale you want as Scale Step - 800 for 1:800 - and a sheet uses exactly that whenever its drawing fits, otherwise the next multiple up. So the three sheets share a scale only when every drawing fits at Scale Step. For a different scale on each, give each component its own Sheet Setup. A scale more detailed than the drawing fits at cannot be forced: choose a larger sheet size instead.
notes.input-panel: Pick a component, set the tier count, and every value it takes appears in one place with its default already filled in - so you can see what a value is and what a normal one looks like before you commit to it. It is not there to reduce how much you have to wire: almost every input already has a default, and the handful that must be wired carry data from upstream, which no panel can stand in for. The bundle it outputs is locked to the component you picked - wire it into a different one and it says so, rather than quietly filling a port that happens to share a name. A wire always wins over the bundle; a value you typed into a port by right-clicking does not, because whatever wins has to be visible on the canvas. Not every component is on its list - a few take one value or none, and a few take things a panel cannot type.
